title: The old men compare two crownings
summary: At Cathair dhearg the court remarks that Ìomhar mac Raghnaill's crowning differs little from his father's eight-and-thirty years before, the same cup passed hand to hand and the same oath said over it, a quiet continuity the custody-book itself gives only a single line apiece.

title: The first silver neck-rings worn
summary: The heads of the seven houses of custody first wear the neck-rings beaten by the smiths of Muileann chiar, so that a stranger at the vein-house or the red hall may know a custodian by the collar at his throat before a word is said.

title: A boy of Inis mhòr asks why the barges keep the coast
summary: Watching the first grain barge loaded on the Abhainn ghorm, a boy of Inis mhòr asks his father why the boat should not simply cross open water by the shorter way, and is answered only with a look and no word, for no one on the island since the fleet has wished to be out of sight of land.

title: The shared meal kept through the cough
summary: When the coughing sickness reaches the reeve's own household at Caol fhiadhaich, his wife refuses to let their door be barred against the shared board, holding that a household which eats apart out of fear will go on eating apart after the fear has passed; she lives, and the custom outlasts the sickness.

title: The king's habit at the gallery's mouth
summary: King Ìomhar takes up a habit no ruler before him is recorded keeping, asking the youngest hand at any gallery he visits to name the prop, the cut and the tally-mark before him; the vein-house's scribe judges it a kind of counting of his own, made by a king with no child to leave the hall to.

title: A singing timber clears the gallery
summary: Bound as a child to a custodian's household, Fearchar mac Lachlainn stands outside a mountain gallery in the night while the custodian, hearing a timber begin to sing, has the working cleared an hour before the prop gives way with no one beneath it; he keeps the memory into his own old age.

title: Am Buabhall Fortanach's new stone walls
summary: Eilidh nic Chaluim raises the burned road-house of Am Buabhall Fortanach again in stone, and a boy of Clann Fhearchair riding out with his father to see the walls going up is given a bowl of the jugged buffalo before the roof itself is finished.

title: Death of Raghnall Beag mac Ìomhair
summary: King Ìomhar's only son, Raghnall Beag, dies of a fever at Cathair dhearg; a custodian of Clann Fhearchair reads the letter aloud and says that a king with no other child is a house with one wall standing, which the wind will find sooner or later.

title: Names cut new on the posts of Dùn ìseal
summary: A young man of Clann Fhearchair, travelling east with his father, stands long before the wooden posts of the spirit-house at Dùn ìseal, reading names the shire itself cuts anew each generation, and says only that a shire which trusts wood to hold its dead must trust its own memory further than he would.

title: The heads of the seven summoned to the capital
summary: With King Ìomhar dead and no living child of his line, riders carry word to all seven houses of custody that their heads are summoned to Cathair dhearg to choose, for the first time since the sunwise turn, a king the crown's own blood cannot simply hand down.

title: Iain mac Lachlainn turns the choosing aside
summary: Named by the other heads as a possible king, Iain mac Lachlainn of Clann Fhearchair turns the honour aside, saying a man who keeps one house's hall well may yet keep a kingdom poorly, and names his own younger brother Fearchar in his place.

title: A borrowed cup for the first oath
summary: With no cup of the crown's own ready for the rite, the head of Clann Mhuirich sends for the cup her own house keeps, so that Fearchar mac Lachlainn drinks his first oath as king from a vessel that belongs, strictly, to one house among the seven rather than to the crown.

title: The double court divided
summary: King Fearchar settles the custom of keeping his court partly at Cathair dhearg and partly at Baile Mòr dhomhain near the vein-house, with his brother Iain keeping Clann Fhearchair's own hall whenever the court is away at the capital.

title: The brothers' leaf-book of letters
summary: A later hand at Baile Mòr dhomhain gathers into one leaf-book the letters King Fearchar and his brother Iain exchange across every season of the divided court, boundary disputes and grain petitions set down beside a long-running complaint over the capital's cooking.

title: A fisherman questioned on the fellowship
summary: Brought before the old king almost by chance, a fisherman of Àth fhiadhaich is kept a full hour answering questions on how boats and nets are shared among the new fellowship's households, and rides home understanding only afterward that the king was asking after the fellowship itself, not the fish.

title: Fearchar Donn asked the child's question
summary: Brought young to the mountain as his father had been, Fearchar Donn is asked at seven years old to name the prop, the cut and the tally-mark before him at a gallery's mouth, and gives an answer his dying father calls, laughing, the first honestly ordinary thing his own house has produced in two reigns.

title: A king's fire kept to the ordinary measure
summary: Dying, King Fearchar asks that no coal be burned beyond the ordinary handful for any rite made over him, and the vein-house keeps the asking to the letter, so that the fire lit for a king is no larger than the fire any house of the seven lights for its own dead.

title: The seven houses stand at Clann Fhearchair's grave
summary: The heads of the seven houses, each still wearing the neck-ring of Muileann chiar, stand at the grave of the king they chose nine-and-twenty years before, and not one of them is heard to say the choosing made in that cold yard was anything other than the right one.
